key_insight: QAOA parameters learned on penalized constrained problems implicitly encode the training penalty weight, creating a resonance effect that makes transfer work best when the deployment penalty matches the original one.
engineering_relevance: For constrained quantum optimization, penalty scaling is not just a modeling choice but a transferability knob, so tuning smaller-|gamma| angle sets and matching penalty weights can improve reuse across instance sizes.
method: Proved that the feasible-subspace probability F(lambda) is a finite real trigonometric polynomial in the penalty weight lambda for any fixed QAOA angles.
Derived resonance, width, and revival predictions from the lattice of frequencies generated by the trained gamma angles.
Validated the theory with exact statevector experiments on a 20-qubit multi-user resource-allocation QUBO.
evidence_signal: Exact statevector simulations on a 20-qubit constrained QUBO confirmed penalty-matched resonance, width scaling, and revival peaks.
watch_item: The result assumes integer-valued penalty violations and exact statevector behavior, so practical performance may shift under noise, non-integer encodings, or hardware constraints.
paper_title: Transferred QAOA Parameters Remember the Penalty Scale: A $λ$-Resonance Law for Constrained Quantum Optimization
